en.title: ch in cherry (/tʃ/)
en.summary: This item illustrates the digraph ch representing the sound /tʃ/ as in the word cherry.

sections.title: Sounds of Ce and Ci
paragraphs: This letter pair is called /tʃe/, /tʃi/. It makes the main sound /tʃ/, as in (ceai) /tʃe/, which means request, petition. This spelling has two sounds in spoken Romanian.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the main sound, press the tip of your tongue behind your top front teeth. Release the air with a soft hiss. Your vocal cords do not vibrate. For the second sound, make this same release while raising the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Hold your hand against your throat to feel that your voice stays silent.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Before the letters e or i, read the sound /tʃ/, as in (cine) /ˈtʃi.ne/. At the end of a word before a faint i, read the soft sound /tʃj/, as in (saci) /satʃʲ/.

sections.title: Useful contrasts
paragraphs: Do not pronounce this group like the hard k sound in cat. You must always say it like the soft sound in church. Keep the sound sharp and quick without adding a full vowel after it at the end of a word.
